text:
maya: FYI CI alert on PR #8345 — microbench `batch_wait_optimizer` regressed ~18% p99 for seq_len=256. See job: https://ci.internal/redwood/8345/build/failed :eyes:
liam: link? stack trace or raw numbers? can you paste the perf diff?
ci-bot: Benchmark `batch_wait_optimizer` (seq=256)
ci-bot: baseline p99=42.1ms, head p99=49.7ms (delta +7.6ms, +18.0%), threshold=+5% -> FAIL
ci-bot: raw output: `bench_results/8345/batch_wait/2026-03-17.txt`
henry: hmm that delta looks like warmup heuristics. last change touched `runtime/batcher/autoscheduler.cc` (commit abc1234).
sasha: can someone run `tools/bench/batch_wait_test --target=ci --seq=256` locally and share flamegraphs? I want KV cache hit rate too.
maya: running now, will post snippets.
maya: local run (head): p99=50.1ms, kv_hit=72%
maya: local run (baseline branch): p99=42.2ms, kv_hit=91%
liam: whoa kv_hit drop from 91% -> 72% is big. that explains token cost and p99. that commit probably changed batch formation thresholds causing early kv-eviction.
henry: commit abc1234 changed `min_batch_latency_ms` logic and introduced a faster path that skips prefix caching for small batches. suspecting cache TTL/hysteresis bug.
sasha: running a git-bisect between baseline~ and HEAD to confirm. will report back.
ci-bot: note: CI golden set used for these microbenches includes a heavy short-seq tail. changes that reduce batching can hurt p99 more than mean.
sasha: bisect result: bad commit is abc1234 (the autoscheduler warmup change). confirmed on both local and ci-emulated setups.
henry: can we do a quick patch to restore previous KV cache retention behavior? or toggle the flag behind a runtime knob?
liam: if we can toggle, we should flip in prod config to avoid rollout impact. but PR merged already — need revert PR or emergency config.
maya: creating revert PR (hotfix/revert-autoscheduler-abcd) and a config knob PR to gate new heuristic. ETA ~20m. :hammer:
devops-bot: Opening incident runbook: https://infra/redwood/incident/INC-2026-172
liam: nice, also add a note to release notes and block today's canary rollout until revert is merged.
maya: agreed — blocking canary. pinging release-engineering. @release-team :warning:
henry: long-term, we should add a microbench variant that exercises KV eviction patterns (short-tail heavy) to catch this earlier. filing an RFC ticket after hotfix.
liam: thanks all. quick followups: - maya post PR link - sasha attach flamegraphs and kv metrics - henry draft a test case for golden set
maya: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/8347 (revert)
sasha: attaching flamegraph: https://graphs.internal/redwood/fg/8345/seq256.png — shows hotpath shift at batcher::select_kernel
liam: :thumbsup: once revert is merged let's re-run CI goldens and un-block rollout.
maya: revert merged, CI re-run queued.
liam: monitoring. thanks everyone.
ci-bot: re-run finished: p99=42.3ms, kv_hit=90.8%, PASS
maya: marking this thread resolved and creating ticket for warmup heuristics follow-up. :white_check_mark:
